sections.h2: What should Brighton owners know before putting a house on the market?
sections.html:
Brighton is a Monroe County town on the southeastern edge of Rochester, and its sales run through the Building and Planning office for zoning paperwork and the Monroe County Clerk for the deed. The Census Bureau estimates 36,695 residents for July 1, 2025, slightly below the 37,137 counted in 2020.

Housing figures for 2020 to 2024 show a 56.4% owner-occupied rate across 15,988 households, a median home value of $282,100 and median gross rent of $1,350. The remaining households rent, and the average household has 2.16 people.

The sections that follow cover the town's layout, what the town expects at a change of ownership, how taxes are billed, and what recording a deed costs in Monroe County.

sections.h2: Where is Brighton and what shaped it?
sections.html:
Brighton spans 15.41 square miles on land and is bordered by Rochester, Irondequoit, Henrietta, Pittsford, Penfield and, across the Genesee River, Chili. English colonists built the first permanent structures around 1790, and the town was formally established in 1814, which makes it one of the oldest towns in Monroe County. Farming and brick-making dominated until the 20th century, when it grew into a residential suburb.

Brighton has no central village. Rochester annexed the old village of Brighton, around East Avenue and Winton Road, in 1905. The commercial hub is Twelve Corners, where Winton Road, Monroe Avenue and Elmwood Avenue cross to form twelve corners, and Brighton High School and Twelve Corners Middle School stand there.

  • The Erie Canal runs through town, along with the Erie Canal Heritage Trail.
  • Lynch Woods Nature Park gives access to the Lehigh Valley Trail.
  • The Brickyard Trail park, built on a former clay-mining site, opened in 2017.

The town sits about 70 miles east of Buffalo and 80 miles west of Syracuse. The Alcoa Care-free Home and the Stone-Tolan House are two older buildings listed on the federal historic register. Trails and parks like these are worth naming in a listing, since buyers ask what is within walking distance.

sections.h2: Who lives in Brighton and what do they pay for housing?
sections.html:
Brighton residents are highly educated. About 68.6% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, median household income is $85,467, and 14.0% of residents were born outside the United States. The poverty rate is 8.9%.

Median owner costs are $2,055 a month with a mortgage and $935 without one. Workers spend 16.9 minutes getting to their jobs on average. About 82.8% of residents had not changed addresses in the past year.

An owner of many years who decides to sell may find the house needs updating that a buyer will price in. Look at what houses on your own street have sold for, and in what condition, before you set an expectation.

Broadband subscriptions reach 91.5% of households and 95.9% have a computer, so most buyers will first meet your house online. Good photos and an accurate listing matter more than printed flyers.

sections.h2: Does Brighton require a certificate of occupancy when a house is sold?
sections.html:
No. The Building and Planning Department says it does not issue a Certificate of Occupancy on a transfer of ownership. Instead it offers a Zoning Verification Letter, which buyers and lenders request when a property changes hands or is refinanced.

The letter states the legal use of the property, the zoning district it is in and, to the best of the office's knowledge, any outstanding violations. You or the buyer's attorney can request it through the form on the town website.

  • The department sits inside the Department of Public Works and enforces the New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code, with extra town requirements for sprinklers.
  • Planning staff also support the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, Conservation Board, Architectural Review Board and Historic Preservation Commission.
  • Land use applications include Certificate of Compliance requests, and permit applications are filed online through the town's OpenGov portal.
  • The town takes payments in person, by phone or by mailed check, not online.

Town Hall at 2300 Elmwood Avenue closed for renovation in November 2024, and town offices have been working from 680 Westfall Road. Confirm the current office location with the town before you drop anything off.

sections.h2: How is property tax billed in Brighton, and what help exists for owners in trouble?
sections.html:
The town's tax office handles the town and county bill and the school tax bill, and the town website has forms to request a bill, a past receipt, or a change to the mailing address and mortgage information. The clerk notes that the first installment of town and county tax is due February 10, and suggests treating January 31 as the real date.

At closing the tax split is worked out between seller and buyer, so request the current bill and a receipt for what has been paid before you sign a contract. Tax receipts for earlier years can be requested through the same page.

Owners behind on a mortgage can call the HOPP hotline, 1-855-466-3456, listed on the town's tax page, or visit homeownerhelpny.com for a referral to a legal services or housing counseling organization. It exists so that no New York family loses a home for lack of a lawyer or counselor.

sections.h2: How much will Monroe County charge to file a Brighton deed?
sections.html:
The Monroe County Clerk is the registrar of deeds for Brighton and records them at 39 West Main Street in Rochester. Same-day recording requires being in line by 4:30 pm, and documents dropped off later are processed the next day. A deed needs an original signature, a notary acknowledgment, a full legal description, and the new tax number.

Monroe County Clerk charges on a residential deed
ItemAmount
One-page deed$50, plus $5 for each added page
TP-584 transfer tax form$5
RP-5217 equalization form (residential)$125
Extra fee on residential deeds$10
Transfer tax$4 per $1,000 of price

Source: Monroe County Clerk, Land Records. A recent change adds a free Restrictive Covenant Modification form, available since June 3, 2026, for removing unlawful discriminatory covenants from recorded documents. Ask your title company whether anything of that kind sits on your deed.

sections.h2: How could you sell a house in Brighton?
sections.html:
Owners here can list, sell privately or take a cash purchase. A well-kept house is simple to market, while a house that needs work, a tenant-occupied property or an inherited home often moves faster with a cash buyer who takes it as-is.

Weigh a cash offer against the net from listing: subtract repairs, agent fees and the months of taxes and utilities you would carry. Use the town's Zoning Verification Letter and a current tax bill as part of your paperwork either way, since both a retail buyer and a cash buyer will want to know the legal use and tax status.

faqs.q: Does Brighton issue a certificate of occupancy when a house sells?
faqs.a: No. The town's Building and Planning office says it does not issue a Certificate of Occupancy at a change of ownership. It issues Zoning Verification Letters on request, which state the legal use, the zoning district and any known violations.

faqs.q: Which office files a Brighton deed?
faqs.a: Record it with the Monroe County Clerk in downtown Rochester. A one-page deed costs $50, each added page costs $5, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms travel with it. Arrive by 4:30 pm for same-day recording.

faqs.q: When is the first installment of Brighton town and county tax due?
faqs.a: February 10. The tax clerk recommends paying by January 31 so you only make one payment each month. The school tax is billed separately, and the town website has request forms for current bills and past receipts.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I pay in Brighton?
faqs.a: At the Monroe County rate of $4 per $1,000, a $250,000 sale produces $1,000. The seller normally pays it. Residences at $1 million or more also carry a 1% extra tax that the buyer pays.

faqs.q: Where do I go if I need help avoiding foreclosure in Brighton?
faqs.a: Call the HOPP hotline at 1-855-466-3456 or visit homeownerhelpny.com. It connects owners with a legal services or housing counseling organization near them, and the town links to it from its tax page.
